blueprints.title: Raised Bed Frame
blueprints.summary: Build a basic wooden frame to grow vegetables off the ground, improving soil quality and drainage.

steps.text: Cut lumber into two 4ft sections and two 8ft sections.
Lay out frame pieces on a flat surface in a rectangle.
Pre-drill holes and drive screws to secure corners.
Staple hardware cloth to the bottom of the frame to block gophers.
Place frame on designated garden bed spot, lay down cardboard layers, and fill with 50/50 topsoil/compost mix.

blueprints.notes: Locate in full sun (6-8 hours daily). Ensure bed is level before filling.
safetyNotes: Watch for splinters when handling untreated timber.
Wear safety glasses during wood cutting.

blueprints.title: Pallet Compost Bin
blueprints.summary: Construct a three-sided square compost bin using recycled shipping pallets.
materials: 4 clean shipping pallets (HT - Heat Treated only, no chemical MB pallets)

steps.text: Select a shady, well-drained spot near the garden.
Stand three pallets on edge to form a three-sided square.
Lash the pallets tightly together at the corners with heavy wire or zip-ties.
Secure the pallets to wood stakes driven into the ground for stability.
Use the fourth pallet as a swing gate or front barrier (removable for turning).

blueprints.notes: A standard 3-bin system is ideal: one for fresh deposits, one active/cooking, and one curing/ready.
safetyNotes: Ensure pallets are marked 'HT' (Heat Treated). Never use 'MB' (Methyl Bromide fumigated) pallets as they leach highly toxic gas.

blueprints.title: Repurposed Glass Window Cold Frame
blueprints.summary: Use an old glass window to build a sloped mini-greenhouse that protects starter plants from early frost.

steps.text: Measure the window frame dimensions.
Build a box using 2x12 lumber matching the window footprint, sloping the sides by cutting a diagonal angle so the back wall is taller than the front.
Screw box sides together and attach window frame to the back wall with hinges.
Set cold frame in a south-facing spot to maximize winter sun.
Place potted seedlings inside during late winter, venting the lid on sunny days.

blueprints.notes: Watch temperature! If sun hits a closed cold frame, temperatures can spike over 100°F (38°C) within minutes, killing seedlings.
safetyNotes: Old windows may contain lead paint; handle with care and sand outdoors.
Ensure the hinges are secure to prevent glass panes from slamming down and shattering.

blueprints.title: Seed Starting Rack
blueprints.summary: Assemble a tiered wooden shelf with adjustable hanging chain grow lights to raise seedlings indoors.

steps.text: Cut vertical posts and horizontal shelf braces from 2x4 studs.
Assemble the ladder-shaped side frames.
Attach horizontal shelf brackets and place cut-to-size plywood shelves.
Mount screw hooks under each shelf to hang chains.
Attach shop lights to chains, keeping them 2-3 inches above growing seedling trays.

blueprints.notes: Ensure lights are plugged into a timer set for 14-16 hours of daily light.
safetyNotes: Route electrical cords safely to avoid contact with watering overflow.
Use a GFC outlet for all indoor seedling grow lights.

blueprints.title: Simple Trellis Panel
blueprints.summary: Build a vertical wooden frame with wire mesh to support climbing plants like peas, beans, and cucumbers.

steps.text: Cut lumber to make two 7ft vertical posts and two 4ft horizontal frames.
Screw the frames together to form a sturdy rectangular panel.
Stretch the hog wire or netting across the frame and staple secure.
Secure the vertical posts deep into the soil behind your garden beds.

blueprints.notes: Position the trellis on the north side of the garden so it does not shade shorter crops.
safetyNotes: Wear work gloves when handling wire mesh to avoid punctures.
Ensure posts are buried deep enough to resist summer wind storms.

blueprints.title: Gravity-Fed Rain Barrel Stand
blueprints.summary: Build an elevated, heavy-duty wooden stand to hold a 55-gallon rain barrel, creating gravity pressure.

steps.text: Clear and level ground beneath a downspout gutter.
Lay cinder blocks flat as a firm, non-settling footprint.
Build a heavy-duty platform using 4x4 legs and 2x6 framing.
Check platform level in both directions.
Place cleaned drum/barrel on top, secure spigot fittings, and connect to gutter downspout diverter.

blueprints.notes: Warning: Water is extremely heavy. A 55-gallon barrel weighs 460 lbs. Stand must be perfectly level and solid.
safetyNotes: Water is heavy: 55 Gallons weighs 460 lbs (208 kg). A weak or unlevel stand collapses easily, creating a severe crush hazard.
Secure the stand to the house wall if possible to prevent tipping.

blueprints.title: First-Flush Diverter
blueprints.summary: Assemble a PVC pipe system that isolates the initial, contaminated dust/debris runoff from the roof.

steps.text: Mount the PVC vertical pipe branch adjacent to your downspout drop.
Install the T-junction so roof water drops straight down into the diversion pipe first.
Insert the float ball inside the PVC pipe (it floats up and seals the inlet when full).
Install the threaded cleanout cap at the bottom with a tiny bleed-hole for slow drainage.
Route the secondary overflow line from the top of the T-junction to fill your rain barrel.

blueprints.notes: The bleed hole allows the diverter to empty slowly after rain, resetting it for the next storm.
safetyNotes: Ensure all PVC joints are thoroughly glued to withstand hydraulic pressure.
Ensure first-flush discharge drains safely away from foundations.

blueprints.title: Sand/Charcoal Emergency Pre-Filter
blueprints.summary: Construct a multi-layer gravity-fed biological sand filter to clarify raw pond or stream water.

steps.text: Drill a hole at the bottom of the bucket and install the spigot spout.
Place a clean cotton cloth or mesh screen at the bottom over the intake.
Add a 3-inch base layer of washed gravel, followed by a 2-inch layer of crushed activated charcoal.
Cover the charcoal with another cotton barrier, then add 6 inches of fine silica sand.
Pour raw water slowly onto the top, ensuring it trickles slowly down through the layers.

blueprints.notes: This clarifies water only. It does NOT sterilize biological pathogens. You must boil or chemically treat water after filtration.
safetyNotes: This is a pre-filter. It only removes particulate matter. It DOES NOT remove microscopic pathogens (viruses, bacteria, giardia). Water MUST be boiled or sanitized before drinking.
Wash all sand and gravel multiple times before assembly.

blueprints.title: Emergency Foot-Pump Handwashing Station
blueprints.summary: Build a hands-free hygiene station using food-grade buckets and a foot-operated bulb pump.

steps.text: Clean both buckets. Mark one for 'Clean Water' and one for 'Greywater'.
Drill a hole in the clean bucket lid for tubing.
Run tubing from the clean bucket bottom to the inlet of the marine foot pump.
Run outlet tubing from the foot pump up to a faucet nozzle secured above the sink basin.
Position the greywater bucket directly beneath the sink basin drain hole.

blueprints.notes: Maintains hygiene during water interruptions. Dispose of greywater safely away from food garden beds.
safetyNotes: Ensure greywater container has a secure lid to avoid mosquito breeding.
Clean the water container regularly to prevent bacterial biofilm build-up.

blueprints.title: Composting Toilet Privacy Stall
blueprints.summary: Build a small outhouse privacy shelter with a double-bucket dry toilet and ventilation stack.

steps.text: Frame a simple 4x4 base floor with 2x4 joists, anchoring to flat blocks.
Build wall frames with a sloped roof header, and sheath with plywood panels.
Install a dry toilet box inside containing a 5-gallon bucket chamber and a urine-diverting funnel.
Run a 3-inch PVC vent pipe from the toilet chamber up through the roof to carry away odors.
Mount the corrugated roofing sheet on top, and attach a simple screen-door latch.

blueprints.notes: Cover deposits with dry sawdust or peat moss after every use to maintain carbon-nitrogen balance and eliminate smell.
safetyNotes: Human waste handling carries biological hazards. Ensure dry cover material (sawdust, peat moss) is used consistently to block flies.
Ensure the ventilation chimney extends past the roof line to pull odor away.
Wear masks and eye protection when cutting pressure-treated lumber.

blueprints.title: Greywater Mulch Basin
blueprints.summary: Dig a mulch-filled filtering trench to process greywater from outdoor kitchen prep or washing.

steps.text: Dig a trench 1.5ft deep and 3ft wide in well-draining soil, sloped away from buildings.
Line the trench sides with geotextile fabric to prevent soil collapse.
Fill the basin bottom with 1ft of coarse organic wood mulch.
Lay the perforated drainage pipe over the mulch to distribute the greywater flow.
Cover the pipe with river rock and clean mulch, feeding sink drain into the pipe inlet.

blueprints.notes: Never feed blackwater (toilet waste) or greasy kitchen sink water directly into a greywater basin.
safetyNotes: Never discharge blackwater (sewage) into greywater systems: it is illegal and creates high pathogen contamination risks.
Ensure the basin is situated at least 100ft away from wells, streams, or open water tables.
Basins must never pooling water: standing water breeds mosquitoes and carries bacteria.

blueprints.title: Heavy-Duty Pantry Canning Shelves
blueprints.summary: Build sturdy, stud-anchored wooden shelves designed to support the immense weight of canning jars.

steps.text: Measure wall space, checking heights and depths (12-inch shelves are best for jars).
Use a stud finder to locate wall framing. Canning jars are very heavy; shelves MUST anchor into studs.
Build upright ladder frames using 2x4 lumber.
Screw shelf supports into ladder uprights and place plywood shelves.
Anchor the entire shelving unit to wall studs using L-brackets to prevent tipping.

blueprints.notes: Standard glass jars should not be stacked directly on top of each other. Build shelf spacing every 8-10 inches.
safetyNotes: Jars are heavy: a shelf of quart jars can weigh over 150 lbs. You MUST secure brackets into structural wall studs, not plaster/drywall alone.

blueprints.title: Root Cellar Double-Pipe Ventilation
blueprints.summary: Install a high-exhaust and low-intake pipe layout to regulate humidity and cooling in a cellar.

steps.text: Plan vent layout: one low intake pipe bringing cool air in, one high exhaust pipe letting warm air out.
Cut PVC pipe sections to fit cellar wall penetrations.
Install intake pipe running down near the floor (within 1ft).
Install exhaust pipe high in the ceiling at the opposite corner of the room.
Clamp fine metal wire mesh over both external pipe openings to block rodents/insects.

blueprints.notes: Use dampers on both pipes to regulate airflow in deep winter. Close vents if outside air is below freezing.
safetyNotes: Confirm cellar structural walls are sound before drilling/excavating penetrations.
Clean mesh filters periodically to prevent blockage and air stagnation.

blueprints.title: Drying Rack / Herb Screen
blueprints.summary: Assemble stackable wooden frames with breathable mesh to dry chamomile, peppermint, or berries.

steps.text: Cut pine slats to build square 2x2ft frames.
Join the corners with small screws and wood glue.
Stretch the food-grade mesh tightly across the bottom of the frame.
Secure mesh with staples every 2 inches and trim excess.
Attach small wooden blocks at the corners to act as spacers for stacking multiple racks.

blueprints.notes: Place racks in a warm, dark, ventilated indoor spot. Direct sunlight burns essential oils in drying herbs.
safetyNotes: Use food-grade mesh; avoid treated industrial plastic screen mesh.
Sand edges to avoid splinters during stacking operations.

blueprints.title: Solar Dehydrator Cabinet
blueprints.summary: Build a black-painted solar collector box that channels warm convection air up through drying racks.
materials: Old glass pane or clear polycarbonate

steps.text: Build a sloped collector box painted black inside, covered with a glass pane.
Frame a vertical cabinet attached to the top of the solar collector.
Install shelf runners inside the cabinet to slide drying racks in.
Drill intake holes at the collector bottom and exhaust holes at the cabinet top.
Cover all holes with fine metal mesh to block insects.

blueprints.notes: Convection draws cool air in, heats it in the collector, and pulls it up through the food trays.
safetyNotes: Food preservation temperatures must stay high enough (130°F-160°F / 54°C-71°C) to prevent mold or bacterial growth. Monitor with a thermometer.

blueprints.title: Small Battery Box Ventilated Shelf
blueprints.summary: Build a sturdy, ventilated wooden enclosure for lead-acid or lithium battery banks.

steps.text: Cut box base and sides, slabbing air vents into the wood sides.
Build a heavy-duty frame to handle battery weight (batteries can exceed 60 lbs each).
Line the interior with acid-resistant coating or heavy plastic sheet.
Install external slotted air vents to allow off-gases to vent outside.
Mount the secure lid, leaving cable penetrations sealed with rubber grommets.

blueprints.notes: Always house batteries in well-ventilated boxes. Lead-acid batteries release explosive hydrogen gas during charging.
safetyNotes: Batteries release highly explosive hydrogen gas when charging: you MUST vent the box to the outside.
Always keep batteries off cold concrete floors by using wood spacers.

blueprints.title: Portable Solar Panel Tilt Stand
blueprints.summary: Build an adjustable, folding wooden stand to mount solar panels at optimal seasonal angles.

steps.text: Build a rectangular wooden frame matching your solar panel perimeter.
Screw the solar panel frame to the wooden mount using small brackets.
Attach support legs to the frame using heavy hinges.
Drill adjustment holes in the legs to set angles for Summer (flat) vs Winter (steep).
Tie down stand using ground anchors and stakes to prevent wind uplift.

blueprints.notes: Tilt angles equal your latitude in Spring/Fall, latitude minus 15 in Summer, and latitude plus 15 in Winter.
safetyNotes: Solar panels act as kites: high winds will blow untethered stands away. Anchor the frame securely to the ground.
Ensure wiring runs are protected inside UV-resistant conduit.

blueprints.title: Rocket Stove Cooking Stand
blueprints.summary: Build a highly efficient outdoor cooking stand using firebricks and a steel casing.
materials: Heavy metal paint can or bucket

steps.text: Cut a hole in the bottom side of the metal can for the feed intake.
Lay firebricks inside to frame an 'L' shaped combustion tunnel.
Fill the gaps between the brick tunnel and can walls with perlite/ash insulation.
Seal the top surface with a thin layer of refractory cement.
Place a heavy cast iron grate over the top chimney opening.

blueprints.notes: Wood burns horizontally in the feed tube, creating draft suction that pulls heat up the vertical chimney.
safetyNotes: For outdoor use only: produces carbon monoxide. Never burn indoors.
Stove becomes extremely hot; keep clear of dry brush and flammable structures.

blueprints.title: Simple Wood Curing Shed
blueprints.summary: Frame a 4x8 wood storage lean-to with open slats to cure firewood while keeping it dry.

steps.text: Mark a level 4x8 footprint on well-drained ground.
Set concrete deck blocks at the corners and level them.
Erect 4x4 posts, ensuring back posts are shorter to create a sloped roof slope.
Frame the rafters and horizontal slats for walls to allow maximum airflow.
Screw metal roof sheets onto the rafters and store split firewood off the wet ground.

blueprints.notes: Ensure walls are open slats. Wood needs wind/airflow to cure properly. Curing takes 6-12 months.
safetyNotes: Shed structures present falling and collapse hazards: verify all framing is securely tied using metal hurricane ties.
Wear steel-toed boots when handling heavy logs and timbers.
Call local utility locators before digging post holes.

blueprints.title: Tarp Rain Porch / Dry Entry
blueprints.summary: Erect a sloped, heavy-duty tarp canopy over a cabin or shelter entry to deflect rain.
materials: Wood poles or telescoping steel poles

steps.text: Identify secure anchor points on the shelter exterior wall.
Secure the back edge of the tarp to the wall hooks, ensuring it is slightly higher than the front.
Extend the front corners of the tarp using support poles.
Tie guy-lines from the poles to heavy rebar stakes driven into the ground at 45 degrees.
Tension all lines to avoid water pooling pockets in the center of the tarp.

blueprints.notes: Always slope the canopy to prevent water accumulation. 1 gallon of pooled water weighs 8 lbs and can tear grommets.
safetyNotes: Wind loads can lift stakes: ensure rebar stakes are driven fully into solid ground.
Periodically check grommet tension; loose tarps collapse under heavy wind or downpours.

blueprints.title: Tool Wall & Sharpening Station
blueprints.summary: Organize wall hooks and set up a workspace vice to sharpen axes, pruners, and shovels.

steps.text: Mount the pegboard/plywood panel securely to workshop wall studs.
Bolt the bench vice firmly onto a sturdy workshop table.
Arrange tool hooks on the panel to hang files, oil, and whetstones.
Place axes/shovels in the vice and file at a 25-degree angle to restore cutting edges.

blueprints.notes: Maintain file teeth by brushing metal shavings out with a file card. Never oil file surfaces.
safetyNotes: Metal filings are sharp: wear safety glasses and leather gloves when filing.
Keep fingers clear of vice jaws during locking.

blueprints.title: Animal Feed Storage Bin
blueprints.summary: Assemble a double-chambered wooden storage chest lined with sheet metal to block rodents.

steps.text: Cut plywood panels for floor, walls, and lid.
Frame the inside edges with 2x2 rails and screw plywood walls together.
Cut sheet metal panels to line the internal floor and walls (prevents mice chewing through).
Secure metal liners inside with short screws.
Attach hinged lid with a locking clasp to keep raccoons out.

blueprints.notes: Place bins off the floor on wood blocks to prevent bottom moisture rot.
safetyNotes: Sheet metal edges are extremely sharp: wear heavy gloves when handling and cutting liners.
Ensure lid latches are tight to avoid finger pinching.

blueprints.title: Small Livestock Waterer Stand
blueprints.summary: Build a stable wooden platform to hold a chicken water bucket equipped with nipple fittings.

steps.text: Build a rectangular 2x4 base stand matching the chicken eye level height (8-10 inches).
Drill 11/32-inch holes in the bottom of the clean 5-gallon bucket.
Thread waterer nipples into the holes, using silicone to ensure a tight seal.
Place bucket on the elevated stand and fill with clean water.
Train flock by tapping nipples to release water droplets.

blueprints.notes: An elevated stand prevents chickens from kicking dirt and feces into their water container.
safetyNotes: Ensure stands are wide enough to prevent tipping if goats or larger animals push against them.
Use only food-grade buckets for livestock water.

blueprints.title: Emergency Field Sink
blueprints.summary: Assemble a gravity-fed sink stand using food-grade barrels, a drainage tray, and a soap dispenser.

steps.text: Build a waist-high wooden frame to hold the dispenser and basin.
Mount the basin in the center of the frame.
Elevate the water dispenser shelf directly behind the basin.
Attach the drain hose to the basin bottom, channeling waste water down into a bucket.
Mount soap dispenser and paper towel holder to the frame uprights.

blueprints.notes: Perfect for field kitchens. Keep clean water bucket separated from greywater bucket.
safetyNotes: Greywater should be disposed of daily to avoid pathogen accumulation.
Ensure soap used is biodegradable if greywater is routed to orchard tree basins.

blueprints.title: Field Binder Wall Station
blueprints.summary: Build a wall-mounted wooden pocket shelf to keep your printed Homemaker Field Binder manuals safe and dry.

steps.text: Cut the pine board to make a bottom ledge (12 inches) and two side rails (14 inches).
Glue and screw the rails together to form a pocket framework.
Attach the plywood backing to the rear of the pocket.
Screw a thin retaining slat across the front of the pocket to hold binder upright.
Mount the station securely to wall studs in a central, dry dry room.

blueprints.notes: Always keep printed manuals in a dry room. In power-down scenarios, the printed Field Binder is your primary guide.
safetyNotes: Ensure screws anchor into wall studs to hold the weight of heavy binders.
Sand all edges to avoid paper tears and splinters.
